styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: Swims, promenade walks and sunsets on the Mediterranean.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Hummus, sabich, Carmel Market and all-night eating.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Bauhaus streets, museums and the old port.

stays.why: Walk to the beach, Rothschild Blvd and the light rail. Best base for first-timers.
Quiet, pretty old streets near the beach and Jaffa. Good for couples.
Old port, flea market and history. Cheaper than the center; light rail links it.
Waterfront promenade, restaurants and parks. Calm and walkable.

food: Try hummus, sabich (fried aubergine pita) and shakshuka. Cheap lunch spots charge about ILS 30–60.
Carmel Market: graze on fruit, cheese and street food. Busiest on Fridays; closed on Shabbat.
Falafel and shawarma are the fast, cheap option, about ILS 20–40 a portion.
Many restaurants are kosher and close from Friday afternoon to Saturday evening. Check opening hours.
Book dinner ahead for Thursday and Friday nights. Tipping is around 10–15%.
more_time: Swap a beach day for Old Jaffa: the port, the flea market and the alleys of the old town.
Add a day in Jerusalem. Buses and trains run often; check times on the day.
Take a half-day to Caesarea or the Carmel coast if you have a car or join a tour.

recommend.why: Three nights lets you swim, eat well and still see Jaffa and the old port without rushing.

month_notes: January: cool and rainy, highs near 17°C. Pack a jacket and an umbrella.
February: still cool and wet, around 18°C. Good for museums and food.
March: warming to 20°C, fewer rainy days. Pleasant for walking.
April: mild and mostly dry, highs near 23°C. Great beach-walk weather.
May: warm at 27°C and almost no rain. Beach season starts.
June: hot and dry, around 29°C. Swim early or late.
July: hot at 31°C with warm nights. Plan shade at midday.
August: hottest month, 32°C. Drink water and use sunscreen.
September: still hot at 31°C but the sea stays warm. Few crowds.
October: cooling to 28°C with a few showers. Very comfortable.
November: mild at 24°C, more rain days. Bring a light rain layer.
December: cool and wet, around 20°C. Quiet season, lower prices.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean climate: hot, dry summers and mild, rainy winters. The beach season runs roughly May to October.

items.title: Best time: April to June and October
items.text: Warm days around 23–29°C with little rain. Ideal for the beach and walking the city.

items.title: Hot, humid summer (July to September)
items.text: Highs of 31–32°C and warm nights. Swim early, rest in the shade at midday.

items.title: Wet winter (December to February)
items.text: Around 10–12 rain days a month and highs of 17–20°C. Pack a jacket and umbrella.

items.title: Rain is seasonal
items.text: Almost none from June to September. Most rain falls between November and March.

items.title: Sea and beach
items.text: The sea is warmest in late summer. Check flags and lifeguard hours on the day.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, hat and sunscreen for summer; a light jacket and rain layer for winter.

transit.best: Walk and bike the center and promenade; use the light rail and buses for longer trips.

modes.text: Since 2023 it links Jaffa, Neve Tzedek, Rothschild Blvd, Sarona and Tel Aviv Center. Handy for the main sights.
Frequent and cheap. Use a Rav-Kav smart card; no cash on buses.
Metered taxis; Gett and Uber work in Tel Aviv. Good for late nights and the airport.
Possible, but traffic is heavy and parking is hard to find. Skip it for city days.
Great along the beach promenade and in the center. The best way to see the city.
Biking is great along the promenade and in the center. Rent by the hour or day.
No ferries to Tel Aviv. Private boats can dock at the marina.
